Rashi on Gittin 49a:10:1.hebrew: אי הכי - דר"ע כר"ש אוקמת ליה, מאי דוחקיך דאוקמת פלוגתא דרישא בשומא דניזק ומזיק? דלמא "לגבות מן העידית" דקאמר ר"ע נמי מעידית דניזק קאמר, דהיא זיבורית דמזיק, כר' ישמעאל; ואמינא: לא פליג עליה אלא בק"ו להקדש, דר' ישמעאל לא סבירא ליה דר"ש בן מנסיא:
Rashi on Gittin 49a:10:1.english: If so - that you have established [the view of] Rabbi Akiva [as being] in accordance with Rabbi Shimon [ben Menasya], what forced you to establish the dispute in the first clause [as concerning] appraising [according to the land] of the injured party or the damager? Perhaps "to collect from the superior-quality land" that Rabbi Akiva says also means from the superior-quality land of the injured party, which is the inferior-quality land of the damager, like Rabbi Yishmael; and I would say [that] he disagrees with him only regarding the a fortiori inference [kal vachomer] for consecrated property [hekdesh], as Rabbi Yishmael does not hold [the view] of Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya:

Rashi on Gittin 49a:12:1.hebrew: אם כן - דלא פליג עליה דרישא, מאי "לא בא הכתוב" דקאמר, דמשמע לא בא לכך אלא לכך:
Rashi on Gittin 49a:12:1.english: If it is so - that he does not disagree with the first clause, what [is the meaning of] "the verse comes only" that he says, which implies [that] it did not come for this [purpose], but rather for that [purpose]?

Rashi on Gittin 49a:12:2.hebrew: ועוד - אי ר"ע קולא קאמר לגבי מזיק, כר' ישמעאל:
Rashi on Gittin 49a:12:2.english: And furthermore - if Rabbi Akiva is stating a leniency regarding the damager, like Rabbi Yishmael:

Rashi on Gittin 49a:12:3.hebrew: מאי קל וחומר להקדש - דקאמר, הואיל וקולא היא, היכי מצי למימר וק"ו דמקילינן נמי גבי הקדש:
Rashi on Gittin 49a:12:3.english: What [is the meaning of] "an a fortiori [inference] for consecrated property" - that [Rabbi Akiva] says? Since it is a leniency [for the damager], how could he say "and [by] an a fortiori [inference]," [meaning] that we are lenient regarding consecrated property as well:

Rashi on Gittin 49a:1:1.hebrew: הכא במאי עסקינן כגון שהיתה עידית דניזק כזיבורית דמזיק - ולרבי ישמעאל נמי אין שמין אכילת ערוגה אלא לפי מה שהיתה — אם שמינה שמינה, אם כחושה כחושה; ולאחר שנישומה בבית דין, ואמר המזיק: אין לי מעות לפורעו, יטול קרקע בדמי מעות נזקו, ובא להגבותו מזיבורית שלו והיא טובה כעידית של ניזק, והלה אומר: מעידית שלך הגביני לפי דמי נזקי, שכן אמרה תורה "מיטב שדהו וגו'":
Rashi on Gittin 49a:1:1.english: With what are we dealing here? [We are dealing with a case] where the superior-quality land of the injured party was equal to the inferior-quality land of the one who caused the damage - According to Rabbi Yishmael as well, we do not appraise the consumption of the garden bed except according to what it was — if [it was] fertile, [as] fertile; if [it was] poor, [as] poor. Rather, [the dispute applies] after it was appraised in court and [the one who caused the damage] said, "I do not have money to pay him; let him take land for the monetary value of his damage," and he comes to pay him from his inferior-quality land, which is as good as the superior-quality land of the injured party, while the other [i.e., the injured party] says, "Pay me from your superior-quality land according to the value of my damage, for thus the Torah said: 'the best of his field, etc.'":

Rashi on Gittin 49a:1:2.hebrew: רבי ישמעאל סבר בדניזק שיימינן - ו"מיטב" שאמרה תורה — שאם בא להגבותו קרקע גרוע מעידיתו של ניזק, ויש לו להגבותו ערוגה במיטב של ניזק, על כרחו יגבהו ממיטב; אבל טובה מעידיתו של ניזק, אין לנו לכוף את המזיק לפרוע, ואפילו יש לו:
Rashi on Gittin 49a:1:2.english: Rabbi Yishmael holds: We appraise [according to that] of the injured party - And [the] "best" [land] that the Torah stated [means] that if [the damager] comes to pay him [the injured party] with land inferior to the superior-quality land of the injured party, and he has [land] to pay him with a plot [equal] to the best of the injured party, against his will he must pay him from [that] best [land]; however, [with land] better than the superior-quality land of the injured party, we do not compel the damager to pay, even if he has [such land].

Rashi on Gittin 49a:1:3.english: We appraise [the land] of the one who caused the damage - The Torah said that he [the injured party] shall collect from him from the best of his [the damager's] fields:

Rashi on Gittin 49a:2:1.hebrew: נאמרה שדה למעלה - לענין נזק, "ובער בשדה אחר":
Rashi on Gittin 49a:2:1.english: “Field” is stated above - regarding damage: “and shall feed in another man’s field”:

Rashi on Gittin 49a:2:2.hebrew: ונאמרה שדה למטה - לענין תשלומין, "מיטב שדהו" וגו':
Rashi on Gittin 49a:2:2.english: And [the word] "field" is stated below - regarding payment: "[Of] the best of his own field," etc.:

Rashi on Gittin 49a:3:1.hebrew: ורבי עקיבא - "שדהו ישלם" כתיב, במשלם הכתוב מדבר, דהיינו מזיק; והכי קאמר ר"ע: לא בא הכתוב להקל על המזיק להפטר בזיבורית שלו אם היא כעידית של ניזק, אלא להגבות לניזקין מן העידית של מזיק:
Rashi on Gittin 49a:3:1.english: And Rabbi Akiva - It is written, "his own field shall he pay" — Scripture is speaking of the one who pays, that is, the damager; and this is what Rabbi Akiva is saying: Scripture did not come to be lenient with the damager, [allowing him] to exempt himself with his inferior-quality [land] if it is [equal to] the best-quality [land] of the injured party, but rather to allow the injured parties to collect from the best-quality [land] of the damager:

Rashi on Gittin 49a:4:1.english: And Rabbi Yishmael - would say to you:

Rashi on Gittin 49a:4:2.hebrew: אהני גזירה שוה - דשדה שדה, דבניזק שיימינן:
Rashi on Gittin 49a:4:2.english: The verbal analogy is effective - [the analogy of] "field" [and] "field," [teaching] that we appraise [the quality of the land] according to [that of] the injured party:

Rashi on Gittin 49a:4:3.hebrew: ואהני קרא - דשדהו ישלם, דמשמע דבמזיק שיימינן:
Rashi on Gittin 49a:4:3.english: And the verse is effective - [referring to] "his field... he shall pay," which implies that we assess [the land] according to the one who caused the damage:

Rashi on Gittin 49a:4:4.hebrew: וזיבורית דידיה לא שויא כעידית דניזק - אהני קרא לשלומי מעידית דידיה, דאי לאו קרא, הוה אמינא לא חייביה רחמנא טפי ממיטב דניזק, ולא רמי דיניה דניזק אעידית דמזיק, ולישקול מאי דמשכח גביה, כאילו לא הוה ליה עידית:
Rashi on Gittin 49a:4:4.english: And his inferior-quality land is not as good as the superior-quality land of the injured party - The verse is effective [to teach that he must] pay from his [own] superior-quality land. For if not for the verse, I would have said [that] the Merciful One did not obligate him [to pay] more than the best [land] of the injured party, and [thus] the injured party's claim does not fall upon the superior-quality land of the one who caused the damage, and he should take [only] what is found with him, as if he did not have superior-quality land:

Rashi on Gittin 49a:5:1.hebrew: וק"ו להקדש - וקא סלקא דעתך בניזקין נמי קאי:
Rashi on Gittin 49a:5:1.english: And an a fortiori inference for consecrated property - And it is currently assumed [that this] also refers to damages:

Rashi on Gittin 49a:8:1.hebrew: לא יהא אלא בעל חוב - בדבורא בעלמא דקביל עליה, מי עדיף מחוב דתנן בבינונית? דאם החמירה תורה בניזקין, לא ילפינן חוב מיניה:
Rashi on Gittin 49a:8:1.english: Let it be no more than a creditor - [Through] a mere verbal [pledge] that he accepted upon himself, is it [superior] to a debt, of which we learned in the Mishnah [that it is collected] from intermediate-quality land? For if the Torah was stringent with regard to damages, we do not derive [the law of] a debt from it:

Rashi on Gittin 49a:8:2.hebrew: איכא למיפרך - כלומר, אפילו סבירא ליה הכי, לא ילפינן הקדש מיניה, דאיכא למיפרך: מה לבעל חוב שהוא הדיוט, דינא הוא דלישקול בעידית:
Rashi on Gittin 49a:8:2.english: It can be refuted - That is to say, even if he [Rabbi Akiva] holds thus, we do not derive [the law of] Temple property from it, because it can be refuted: What [comparison can be made] to a creditor, who is an ordinary person — it is logical that he should collect from superior-quality land:

Rashi on Gittin 49a:8:3.english: For Scripture enhanced his power with regard to damages - that his fellow is liable for his damage:

Rashi on Gittin 49a:9:1.hebrew: משלם נזק שלם - ודריש "רעהו" הכי: "רעהו" הוא דמשלם חצי נזק, אבל להקדש נזק שלם. ולגבי הזיק הקדש דריש הכי: ל"רעהו" הוא דמחייב, אבל הקדש שהזיקה פטור:
Rashi on Gittin 49a:9:1.english: Pays full damages - And he expounds [the term] "his neighbor's" thus: [for goring] "his neighbor's" [ox], one pays half damages, but to consecrated property, [one pays] full damages. And regarding [a case where] consecrated property caused damage, he expounds [it] thus: [an ox belonging] to "his neighbor" is liable, but consecrated property that caused damage is exempt:

Tosafot on Gittin 49a:11:1.hebrew: ורבי עקיבא סבר לה כר"ש בן מנסיא - ואם תאמר: בפ"ק דבבא קמא (דף ה.), דפרכינן: "וליתני תרי גווני שור", ומשני: "הא תבריה ר"ע לגזיזיה" — אכתי תיקשי לו: דליתני שור דאזיק הדיוט ושור דאזיק הקדש, דדינייהו חלוקין אליביה! וי"ל: דבהקדש לא קמיירי. וא"ת: אכתי איכא למיפרך: מה להדיוט, שכן יפה כחו בנזקי אדם ובור, תאמר בהקדש שהורע כחו באדם המזיק, ד"כי יאכל" — פרט למזיק, ובור — דכתיב (שמות כ״א:ל״ד): "והמת יהיה לו", שהמת שלו! וי"ל: דאיכא למיעבד ק"ו הכי: מה קרן הדיוט דקיל, דתם אינו משלם אלא ח"נ, גובה במועד מן העידית, קרן הקדש דחמיר לא כ"ש:
Tosafot on Gittin 49a:11:1.english: And Rabbi Akiva holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya - And if you say: In the first chapter of Bava Kamma (5a), where [the Gemara] raises the objection: "Let [the Mishnah] teach two types of ox," and answers: "Rabbi Akiva already broke his shearings [i.e., retracted his objection]," it should still be difficult for it: let [the Mishnah] teach an ox that damaged [the property of] a common person and an ox that damaged [the property of] the Temple treasury, since their laws are different according to him! And one can say: [The Mishnah] is not dealing with Temple treasury [property]. And if you say: Still, one can refute [the a fortiori inference]: What [is unique] to a common person? [It is] that his rights are strong regarding damages of a person [who damages] and a pit; can you say [the same] regarding the Temple treasury, whose rights are weakened regarding a person who damages — for [the verse] "when he eats" excludes one who damages — and [regarding] a pit, as it is written (Exodus 21:34): "and the dead [animal] shall be his," [meaning] that the dead [animal] is his! And one can say: One can construct the a fortiori inference like this: If [in the case of] goring of a common person, which is lenient — in that an innocuous [ox] pays only half-damages — [yet when] forewarned it collects from superior-quality land, [then in the case of] goring of the Temple treasury, which is stringent, is it not all the more so:

Tosafot on Gittin 49a:12:1.hebrew: ועוד מאי ק"ו להקדש - פי' בקונטרס: הואיל ו"מן העידית" דקאמר ר"ע אניזק קאי, ולאקולי אתא, דיהיב ליה מזיק מזיבורית, אם כן מאי ק"ו להקדש? גריעותא הוא! וקשה, דמ"מ איצטריך ק"ו דמשלם ממיטב דניזק ולא מזיבורית דניזק. ונראה דה"פ: מאי "קל וחומר להקדש"? דלענין לחיובי מזיק בהקדש לא קאמר, דהא מ"רעהו" נפקא כדדריש ר"ש בן מנסיא, אלא לענין מיטב קאמר, ולא הוה ליה לר"ע לאהדורי לרבי ישמעאל ק"ו, כיון שר' ישמעאל עצמו היה מודה בכך אי לאו משום דפטר ליה לגמרי. וה"ר שלמה מרודוש תירץ דה"פ: מאי "ק"ו להקדש"? דשיימינן בעידית דניזק ולא בדמזיק — מי ידעינן עידית דהקדש? שמא יש להקדש עידית בסוף העולם טובה שאין כמוה! ועל כרחיך בדמזיק שיימינן, דלא שייך כלל למישם בדניזק:
Tosafot on Gittin 49a:12:1.english: And furthermore, what [is the meaning of] an a fortiori [inference] to consecrated property - Rashi explained: Since "from the best" that Rabbi Akiva says refers to the injured party and comes to be lenient [on the damager], as the damager gives him from [the damager's] inferior-quality land, if so, what [is the meaning of] "an a fortiori [inference] to consecrated property"? It is a disadvantage! And this is difficult, because even so, an a fortiori [inference] is needed [to teach] that he pays according to the best of the injured party and not according to the inferior-quality [land] of the injured party. And it seems that this is its explanation: What [is the meaning of] "an a fortiori [inference] to consecrated property"? For regarding obligating a damager for consecrated property, [Rabbi Akiva] is not saying [it], as that is derived from "his fellow's," as Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya expounds; rather, he is saying [it] regarding [paying from] the best, and Rabbi Akiva should not have responded to Rabbi Yishmael with an a fortiori [inference], since Rabbi Yishmael himself would have agreed to this were it not for the fact that he exempts [damages to] it completely. And Rabbi Shlomo of Rodosh answered that this is its explanation: What [is the meaning of] "an a fortiori [inference] to consecrated property"? [If you say] that we appraise according to the best [land] of the injured party and not according to that of the damager — do we know the best [land] of consecrated property? Perhaps consecrated property has best [land] at the end of the world, so good that there is none like it! Perforce we appraise according to [the land of] the damager, for it is not relevant at all to appraise according to [the land of] the injured party:

Tosafot on Gittin 49a:1:1.hebrew: כגון שהיתה עידית דניזק כזיבורית דמזיק - ואיפכא לא מצי למימר, דכ"ע מודו דאינו נותן אלא מעידית שיש לו, ואינו חייב לקנות, כדאמרינן בפ"ק דבבא קמא (דף ז:): אין לו אלא זיבורית, כולן גובין מן הזיבורית. ומיהו אי בשל עולם הן שמין לר"ע, הוה מצי למימר כגון דאית ליה למזיק עידית בינונית וזיבורית, וזיבורית דידיה כעידית דעלמא, ועידית דידיה כעידית דניזק. ואפילו למאן דאמר בשלו הן שמין, הוה מצי למימר דאיכא בינייהו כגון דעידית דמזיק כזיבורית דניזק, דלמ"ד "או כסף או מיטב", משלם כסף לר' ישמעאל, ולר"ע משלם מיטב שלו:
Tosafot on Gittin 49a:1:1.english: For example, where the superior-quality land of the injured party was equal to the inferior-quality land of the one who caused the damage - And [the Gemara] could not say the reverse, because everyone agrees that he only pays from the superior-quality land that he possesses, and he is not obligated to buy [other land], as we say in the first chapter of Bava Kamma (7b): [If] he has only inferior-quality land, all [creditors] collect from the inferior-quality land. However, if according to Rabbi Akiva we appraise [the land] by [the standard of] the world [at large], [the Gemara] could have said [that the dispute is in a case] where the one who caused the damage has superior-, intermediate-, and inferior-quality land, and his inferior-quality land is equal to the superior-quality land of the world [at large], and his superior-quality land is equal to the superior-quality land of the injured party. And even according to the one who says we appraise by his [own holdings], [the Gemara] could have said that there is [a practical difference] between them in a case where the superior-quality land of the one who caused the damage is equal to the inferior-quality land of the injured party; for according to the one who says "either money or the best [land]," he pays money according to Rabbi Yishmael, whereas according to Rabbi Akiva he pays [with] his own best [land]:

Tosafot on Gittin 49a:6:1.hebrew: שור רעהו אמר רחמנא ולא שור של הקדש - תימה, אמאי לא מוקי לה בשן ורגל שהזיק את ההקדש, דהתם לא כתיב "רעהו", ומקרן ליכא למילף, שכן אינה מועדת מתחילתה; וגזירה שוה ד"תחת" "נתינה" "ישלם" "כסף" לא נתקבלה אלא לענין מיטב דוקא, ולא לענין תשלומין, דאי לכל מילי, א"כ נפטרו כולהו ברשות הרבים, וכלים, ושור פסולי המוקדשים, וטמון! וי"ל: כיון דכתיב "רעהו", תו ליכא למילף מיטב בשן ורגל שהזיק את ההקדש מק"ו דהדיוט, דאיכא למיפרך: מה להדיוט שכן יפה כחו לענין קרן! וכה"ג פריך בסמוך: "שכן יפה כחו בניזקין". וכי קאמר "אלא באומר הרי עלי מנה וכו'", לא בעי לאוקמא בשן ורגל, משום דמנזקין אנזקין אסיק אדעתיה שפיר דאיכא למיפרך "שכן יפה כחו", אבל מנזקין אמלוה לא הוה סלקא דעתיה למיפרך; דהא כי מוקי לה כר"ש בן מנסיא, לא פרכינן "מה להדיוט שכן יפה כחו לענין ריבית ואונאה" אנזקין. ועוד יש לומר דכולהו נזקין פטורין בהקדש, כדמוכח בירושלמי בריש פרקא, דאמר: במה אנן קיימין? אי בהכשר נזקין — הא תנינא: "שור רעהו" ולא שור של הקדש! ואי בנזקי גופו — הא תני רבי חייא: נזקין להדיוט, ואין נזקין לגבוה! אלא באומר הרי עלי מנה כו'. משמע דלא משכח נזקין להקדש, לא בשן ורגל ולא באדם המזיק. ובפ"ק דבבא קמא (דף ט:) נמי תנן: נכסים שאין בהן מעילה; ואכולהו ד' אבות קאי, ואפילו אנזקי אדם, למ"ד "מבעה" זה אדם. והא דמשמע בפרק השואל (ב"מ דף צט:) דאדם המזיק את ההקדש חייב לשלם קרן, היינו מדרבנן. וא"ת: והא הקדש יליף מתרומה, דכתיב בה (ויקרא כב) "כי יאכל" — פרט למזיק; והתם בתרומה חייב לשלם קרן, דמזיק ממון כהן הוא! וי"ל: דאע"ג דבתרומה חייב לשלם, מ"מ לא מהאי קרא מפיק, אלא מקרא אחרינא, דהוי כגוזל חבירו ומזיקו. והשתא כולהו נזקין דפטירי בו בהקדש ילפינן מאדם, דיותר ראוי לחייב אדם המזיק בידים ממזיק ע"י כריית בור או שולח בעירו. וא"ת: א"כ, "רעהו" דכתב רחמנא למה לי? וי"ל: דאי לאו דאשכחן בחד דוכתא דפטר רחמנא להדיוט בהקדש לגמרי, לא הוה דרשינן "כי יאכל" פרט למזיק, אלא לפטור מחומש לחודיה:
Tosafot on Gittin 49a:6:1.english: The Merciful One states “another’s ox,” and not an ox that is consecrated property - It is puzzling: why does [the Gemara] not establish it [i.e., Rabbi Akiva’s a fortiori inference] in [a case of] tooth or foot [damage] that damaged consecrated property, where “another’s” is not written? And one cannot derive [an exemption there] from horn [damage], because [horn] is not forewarned from the outset; and the verbal analogy of “instead,” “giving,” “he shall pay,” [and] “silver” was only received [by tradition] specifically regarding [paying from] superior-quality land, and not regarding [the laws of] payments — for if [it applied] to all matters, then all of them [all the other categories of damage] would be exempt in the public domain, and [for] utensils, and [for] an ox of disqualified consecrated animals, and [for] concealed items! And one can say: Once “another’s” is written [regarding horn], one can no longer derive [payment from] superior-quality land for tooth and foot [damage] that damaged consecrated property from an a fortiori inference from an ordinary person, because one can refute [it]: What [is unique] about an ordinary person? That his power is enhanced regarding horn [damage]! And similarly, [the Gemara] refutes [the inference] immediately below: “That his power is enhanced regarding damages.” And when [the Gemara] says, “Rather, [it refers] to one who says: It is incumbent upon me [to donate] one hundred dinars, etc.,” it did not want to establish it in [a case of] tooth and foot [damage], because from damages to damages it readily occurred to him [the questioner] that one can refute [it with] “that his power is enhanced,” whereas from damages to a loan it would not have occurred to him to refute [it]; for indeed, when [the Gemara] establishes it in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya, we do not refute [the inference] to damages [by saying] “What [is unique] about an ordinary person? That his power is enhanced regarding interest and overcharging.” And furthermore, one can say that all damages are exempt in [the case of] consecrated property, as is evident in the Jerusalem Talmud at the beginning of the chapter, where it says: What are we dealing with? If with indirect property damages — behold, we learned: “Another’s ox,” and not an ox of consecrated property! And if with bodily injuries [caused by a person] — behold, Rabbi Ḥiyya taught: Damages [apply] to an ordinary person, and there are no damages for the Most High! Rather, [it refers] to one who says, “It is incumbent upon me [to donate] one hundred dinars, etc.” This implies that it does not find [liability for] damages to consecrated property, neither in tooth and foot [damage] nor in a person who causes damage. And in the first chapter of Bava Kamma (9b) as well, we learned in a Mishnah: “Property that is not subject to misappropriation of consecrated property”; and it refers to all four primary categories [of damage], and even to bodily injuries caused by a person, according to the one who says mav’eh [in the Mishnah] refers to a person. And as for that which is implied in the chapter [entitled] HaSho’el (Bava Metzia 99b), that a person who damages consecrated property is obligated to pay the principal — that is by rabbinic decree. And if you say: But consecrated property is derived from terumah, regarding which it is written (Leviticus 22[:14]), “when he eats” — excluding one who damages [it]; and there, regarding terumah, one is obligated to pay the principal, because he is damaging the property of a priest! And one can say: Even though regarding terumah one is obligated to pay, nevertheless it is not derived from this verse, but from another verse, since it is like one who robs his fellow and damages his [property]. And now, all [the other categories of] damages that are exempt therein regarding consecrated property we derive from a person [who causes damage], for it is more fitting to obligate a person who causes damage directly with his hands than one who causes damage by digging a pit or sending out his fire. And if you say: If so, why do I need “another’s” that the Merciful One wrote? And one can say: Because if not for the fact that we found in one place that the Merciful One completely exempted an ordinary person [for damage] to consecrated property, we would not have expounded “when he eats” [as] excluding one who damages [altogether], but rather to exempt [him] from the [added] fifth alone:
